_about: The Magic Portals port's rolling stones and barrel blasts: what a stone breaks, when it
counts as touching, and what a blast breaks. See docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-

_note: Entity names a rolling stone breaks whether or not the placement sets
metadata/breakable. The Godot project breaks only what the flag marks (hazards.gd:117-120).
Eight breakable_wall placements carry no flag: levels 8, 12, 18, 21 (two), 23 and 24
of chapter 1, and level3a. That is the original's own scene data, not the converter:
each is an inline entity in its .esc whose CustomData lacks breakable, and Ethanon
reads an inline entity as it stands (ETHEntityProperties.cpp:202-224). So the
original decides by something the data does not show. The owner played it, and on
11 September confirmed that stones broke those walls.
DECODED since (planning step 115): the stone's side is ETHBeginContactCallback_breakable_wall
(MiscCallbacks, listing L68341), which Ethanon binds by the ENTITY's name (ETHASUtil.cpp:63-67)
and which never reads 'breakable': #1-14 tests the other body's 'demolisher', #16-33 its
speed against scale(1.5), #35-40 destroy(thisEntity). So every breakable_wall, flagged or
not, breaks for a stone - the owner's testimony, from the bytecode - ABOVE the speed gate and
by a stone's BEGIN of contact only (the wall block below, planning step 175). The flag is read only
by isBreakable (L67923), which is a blast's grab (the blast block below).
breakable._source: owner testimony, 11 September 2026; ETHBeginContactCallback_breakable_wall (listing L68341) #1-40, planning step 115

_note: What a rolling stone does to the PLAYER it begins to touch (planning step 160, STK). ETHBeginContactCallback_rolling_stone
(listing L68515, MiscCallbacks bytes 346486..347456) #107-129: where isCharacter(other) - the player is the only
entity with that datum (GameCharacter::GameCharacter L22977, built by one class, MainCharacter) - and the stone's
hitIntensity is above 2.5 (CMPIf against 0x40200000, JNP skips, so STRICTLY above), other.SetInt('hp', 0): the same
write a death area makes (L66942 #9-18), so the death is a death area's - blood, the player hidden, the lost screen,
no sound of its own (GameStateController::checkGameLost L23649 #3-63). hitIntensity is #6-56:
dp2(the STONE's own GetLinearVelocity, normalize(other.GetPositionXY() - thisEntity.GetPositionXY())) / getScale()
- the stone's speed toward the player's entity point, over 50 px a unit (D11_check C47: 2.5 is 125 level units a
second of the original's physics). A stone at rest (#34-35: length 0 skips the whole callback) or moving away kills
nothing, and the player's own movement is not in the number. A begin-contact only. The stone is untouched. Carried by
rolling_stone.ent in both spellings, placed, launched or dropped by the beholder - not rolling_stone_no_emissive.ent
(2-30), which has no callback of its own. The beholder's rocks are the same callback, and the port kills with them in
Boss::Contacts (boss.json rock.crush_intensity, the same 2.5), which this does not replace.
The number the port tests is the impact watch's, the one the stone's own shake reads (Impacts::Begin::Approaching):
the fastest the stone came along that line since it last met or left something. INFERRED equal to the callback's, not
measured: no footage shows a stone against the player (docs/parity-backlog.md STK-1).

_note: ETHBeginContactCallback_breakable_wall (MiscCallbacks, listing L68341, bytes 345591..345993) decoded WHOLE (planning
step 175; GAMEPLAY). It is the wall's side of a contact, run by Box2D's step when a pair first touches
(ETHContactListener.cpp:87-105, called from b2Contact.cpp:228 before the step's solver), for the wall AND for the
other body, and the other body's own callback is a separate function (rolling_stone's, demolish.json stone):
#1-14   `if (other.CheckCustomData('demolisher') == DT_NODATA) return`: only a body with the datum does anything.
The census (out/parity/program/WALL/census.md) finds it on rolling_stone.ent and rolling_stone_no_emissive.ent
and on no other entity file or placement in the 128 levels.
#16-33  hit = other.GetPhysicsController().GetLinearVelocity().length(), against g_scale.scale(1.5f): CMPf v3 v8,
JNP -> #65, so a speed EQUAL to the gate or below it skips everything that follows. STRICTLY above.
GetLinearVelocity is Box2D's m/s over the global scale, which is 1 (ETHPhysicsController.cpp:117-123;
00_order 8.0 rule 5); scale(1.5) is 1.5 x SGlobalScale.m_scaleFactor (listing L158); a body's Box2D
velocity is its level units a second x that factor / 50 (ETHPhysicsSimulator.cpp:27: 1 m = 50 raw px,
raw px = level units x the factor), so the factor cancels: the gate is 1.5 m/s of the ORIGINAL's own
physics = 75 level units a second (D11_check C40 reads it the same). Nothing is divided by getScale here
(the stone's own hitIntensity is, #6-56) and no projection is taken: the WHOLE velocity's length.
#35-40  destroy(thisEntity): sets the datum `destroy` = 1 (listing L68753); the wall's own callback
(ETHCallback_breakable_wall #1-86, blast below) deletes it with its dust, the same frame.
#42-60  `if (other.GetUInt('destroyable') == 1) destroy(other)`: CMPIu v8, immediate 1 (00_order 8.0 rule 1), JNZ
skips - EXACTLY 1, not any non-zero. ETHCallback_rolling_stone #0-44 then adds rolling_stone_destroy.ent at
the stone's point (effects.json rolling_stone_destroy) and deletes it, the same frame.
#61-64  startEarthquake(30, 200), in the same arm (the first argument is the last pushed): a slow touch does NOTHING
- no break, no death, no shake.
The port judges each (wall, stone) pair AT ITS BEGIN, as the callback is called, and reads that ONE begin at up to TWO
instants - a PORT INFERENCE, not a decode: the original's callback runs once, and the port's solver brakes a closing pair
before it meets, so each reading is an under-estimate of Box2D's velocity and the LARGER judges (planning step 175, fix 2).
first look: the stone comes within contact.margin_px of the wall's box and was not within it after the last tick
(Demolish::State::touching): the speed the contact watch says it carried (Impacts::Watch::Carried, the fastest it
came along the line to the wall since it last met or left something: Impacts.hpp), over SimRatio;
AND (planning step 218) the same look is taken a step early for a stone the engine's brake held SHORT of the wall: the engine
moves a body and then solves its contacts and brakes a pair that stands inside the two bodies' travel in the step, so a stone
that rolls at a wall ends the step 1 to 6 units from it (measured: 1.0 to 6.25 over the 117 variants of 1-22's gold route, all within
one step's travel of the wall) with its velocity taken out, and never comes within margin_px again until it creeps up at 0.1 m/s.
Box2D takes the position first too and finds the pair touching at the START of the next step with the velocity the stone still
carries, so the callback reads that. The port reads such a stone now, when the velocity it carried INTO the step, along the line
to the wall, over the step (ScriptClock simS), reaches the wall's margin from where the step left it: Demolish::State::Tick's
`simS`, Contact::braked, and the log's 'held short of the wall by the engine's brake'. Without it the second stone of 1-22 held
the wall at 0.12 m/s (the owner's report of 2026-11-05). A slow stone is still judged by the gate; a stone moving along the wall or
away from it is not looked at; 11 of 117 tap variants of the gold route won before, 115 do now.
second look: the stones' watch finds the pair begun within Box2D's skin (earthquake.json impacts.touch_px, Level::stoneWatch,
read before the wall can be taken): Impacts::Begin::Approaching, which for a stone that came through the air is the
free flight's replay of what Box2D's own step reads (planning step 162; the layer's impact watch reads the same
contact so). A second look that holds again changes nothing; one that breaks the wall the first held does.
Judging only at the second look was tried and dropped: 1-22's first stone, within the margin of its wall at 3.162 m/s on
tick 308, lands at the wall's foot and is within the skin on tick 320 at a creep. A stone that begins to touch a wall slowly
and is later pushed faster while still touching does not break it: no second begin. A body that is not a breakable_wall is
not this callback's (a carranca is a separate row of docs/parity-backlog.md): it keeps the touch rule above.

_note: How near a stone must come to a breakable's box to touch it. The Godot project's stone
breaks what it touches (body_entered), and a solver leaves a body resting against a
wall touching it rather than overlapping it, so the port's overlap test grows the
box by this much. A threshold of the port's, not a measurement.
What a barrel bomb's blast breaks. explode (MiscCallbacks, listing L67590) grabs with an
EntityGrabber of radius scale(80) filtered by isBreakableOrExplosiveOrBurnable (#33-47;
fire.json blast.radius_px), keeps each entity whose first contact on the line from the
blast is itself (#63-109, getFirstContactExcept with NonProjectileChooser), and sets its
'destroy' to 1 (#111-122). isBreakable (L67923) is GetUInt('breakable') != 0: the FLAG,
never the name, so the eight flagless breakable_walls above are not grabbed as
breakables. ETHCallback_breakable_wall (L68771) #1-86 reads isDestroyed and deletes the
wall with its wall_destroy and startEarthquake(20 x destroyEffectScale), the same frame:
the barrel's callback is a dynamic entity's, the wall's a static one's, and
ETHScene::Update runs the static entities' callbacks after the dynamic ones'
(ETHScene.cpp:464-491). Footage F6 (2-12) shows the wall gone in the frame
explosion_large first shows (#160).
entities: the breakables whose own callback reads isDestroyed and takes the entity: the
breakable_wall's (ETHCallback_breakable_wall) and, since planning step 223, the
carrancas' (carrancaCallback L85350 #123-157, called by ETHCallback_carranca and
ETHCallback_carranca_right: carranca_destroy.ent, startEarthquake(20, 0), DeleteEntity),
each in either spelling (callbacks bind by RemoveExtension of the name, 00_order 8.0 rule 4).
Step 223: 2-15 has two crystals inside two carrancas' colliders that the designers' barrels
free; a blast 30 and 40 u from them (radius 80) took neither before.
